## INIT2 · INIT2-manifest-rules — INIT2: handed badges, R33's spelling, the dev key's home, R34's domains, and the implementer's defaults

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 5

Evidence: All five ruled by the Architect (.wash/local/INIT2-questions-1-ruling.md): Q1 handed items carry {endpoint, badge} below FIRST_MINTED_BADGE, minted by init; Q2 root/system/users reserved, naming one refused as a budget grant (R33); Q3 DEV_PUBLIC_KEY moves to libs/signing, K16 confirmed no collision; Q4 confinement by kind without cores after the owner's decision on INIT2-confined-cores (pages on main 1d109ac5f); Q5 defaults accepted with three notes. Forwarded to INIT2's implementer with the page lines; checked at INIT2's review.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `a6b0a72cc69cc132b63b33169a91962f` · 2026-10-02T23:45:14Z

> Five questions from INIT2's implementer before deliverable 1's checks are final; detail, options and its recommendations in ./.wash/local/INIT2-questions-1.md. Q1 (blocks badge minting and bucket counts): `handed` lists endpoint names only, but servers' args name the badges their callers carry and init never reads args. Rec: each handed item is {endpoint, badge} below FIRST_MINTED_BADGE, unique per endpoint; one handed item = one root badge = one system caller. Q2 (R33's spelling): unknown members are parse errors already, so how does a manifest 'grant a budget handle'? Rec: root/system/users reserved; a receives or handed item naming one is refused with R33's reason. Q3: DEV_PUBLIC_KEY lives in loader/src/verify.rs, a module of the loader binary, which is K16's. Rec: move it into libs/signing, verify.rs uses it by name (K16 lands the one line). Q4 (R34): the manifest does not say which domains a server serves. Rec: domains = each server entry and each principal label set; a server's users = servers handed its endpoints plus every principal domain if shared; kinds checked in order (endpoint, volume, network, device, instance, cores); a device held by two servers or an endpoint received by two always refused. Q5 (defaults): buckets checked only where args carry buckets=; init a system caller at keyd/consoled/bootfsd; the INIT_PAGES bound counts the largest launch's transients and an exit endpoint per server; login keys 'ssh-ed25519 <base64>' decoded to 32 bytes, no crypto. The implementer builds the rest meanwhile, each open rule behind one function. Page lines with each ruling, please.

### Orchestrator · Progress

Event: `37aff4ca853230b02646227f937e0f4d` · 2026-10-03T00:00:32Z

> For your awareness, four implementation choices I ruled for INIT2's deliverable 2 (detail .wash/local/INIT2-questions-2.md): (a) init passes bootfsd the manifest's public names after the entry's own args, per bootfsd.md, and sizes its startup block with them; (b) ruling 1's fixed arena: libs/rt gets Heap::fixed(base, len) and a feature so init installs its own instance over one map_anon of ARENA_PAGES, every other program's allocator unchanged; (c) init calls DeviceInfo through redoubt_sys::syscall directly, no rt wrapper; (d) root's budget_usage is read before the arena is mapped and the whole bound, arena included, is compared against that free, so the arena is not counted twice. Say on this thread if any crosses a page you read differently; otherwise they stand.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `13aa817ad7d255652e4709638d9e97d3` · 2026-10-03T00:02:04Z

> Rulings, with exact page lines, are in ./.wash/local/INIT2-questions-1-ruling.md.
> 
> Q1: A. Each handed item is {endpoint, badge}. The badge is a decimal string below FIRST_MINTED_BADGE, unique per endpoint. init mints it from the handed item and never reads it from an argument. One handed item is one root badge, which is one system caller.
> Q2: A. root, system and users are reserved names. A receives or handed item that names one is refused as a budget grant (R33).
> Q3: A. DEV_PUBLIC_KEY moves into libs/signing, and verify.rs uses it by name. That is one loader line, and the loader is K16's: please get K16's nod, then INIT2 lands the move in one commit.
> Q4: Waiting on the owner. They asked what a confined boot is and whether to pause it, and I am putting that to them now. INIT2 builds nothing more of R34 until they answer. Ruled now, because it does not depend on confinement: in every manifest, a device entry held by two servers is refused, and so is an endpoint that two servers receive on.
> Q5: Defaults accepted, with three notes:
> - init reads only buckets=N from the arguments, using the serving library's parser.
> - The INIT_PAGES bound's per-object constants are pinned by a host test against objects.md. The six-server case fails if root's usage after the boot exceeds the bound.
> - Keys are ssh-ed25519 only. Any other form is a manifest error.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `8f3ea5b832111cb0fffc869ea359220b` · 2026-10-03T00:06:08Z

> Q4 is now ruled, after the owner's decision on INIT2-confined-cores (no core rule; the check is built in INIT2; pages at 1d109ac5f). It is the implementer's option A without the cores function. The kinds are checked in the order endpoint, volume, network, device, server instance, and each refusal names its kind. A server's users are the servers handed one of its endpoints plus, for a shared server, every principal domain: the same count as the bucket rule. Steward and sshd are exempt by program name, untested until the steward step. The page lines are in .wash/local/INIT2-questions-1-ruling.md Q4. All five questions are answered. INIT2 should rebase onto main for 1d109ac5f before writing init.md.
